local.sub: Photos come from a folder ({env}) instead of Immich. Results are written to an XMP file next to each photo (hierarchical keywords and description), read by digiKam, darktable, Lightroom Classic, Bridge and Immich; the photos themselves are never modified.
local.sub_darktable: Photos come from the darktable library, read without ever being changed. Results are written to each photo's XMP file (photo.nef.xmp, and the one of each duplicate); darktable picks them up at startup if « look for updated XMP files on startup » is on (Preferences > storage). Photos are never changed.
local.sub_lightroom: Photos come from the Lightroom Classic catalog, read without ever being changed (with Lightroom closed). Results are written to photo.xmp next to RAW files; in Lightroom, Metadata > « Read Metadata from Files » picks them up. First turn on « Automatically write changes into XMP » (Catalog Settings) so your edits are not lost when reading. JPEG, TIFF, HEIC and DNG files are never changed: Lightroom will not see keywords on them.
local.sub_rapidraw: Photos come from a folder opened in RapidRAW. Results are written to photo.xmp next to each photo; RapidRAW adds them to its keywords when XMP sync is on. It never removes any: a keyword removed here (rejected detection) must be removed in RapidRAW too.
local.sub_rawtherapee: Photos come from a folder opened in RawTherapee. Results are written to an XMP file next to each photo, never to its .pp3 files; RawTherapee uses them on export if Preferences > Metadata > « XMP sidecar synchronization » is set to “read”. Photos are never changed.

set.analysis_window.sub: Automatic analysis of new photos only runs within this window (server time). The Sync button ignores it.
set.analyze_videos.sub: The key frame of each video, chosen by Immich, is analyzed like a photo (camera traps, wildlife videos). One frame per video.
set.auto_confirm.sub: Rule: confidence above the threshold, species observed nearby and no other credible candidate. Calibrated: only when your reviews are enough to guarantee 98% precision.
set.auto_confirm_audit.sub: Share of detections that would have been auto-confirmed, kept for review (“Spot check” filter): your answers measure the actual reliability of auto-confirmation and refine its calibration.
set.auto_confirm_max_runner_up.sub: Above this, the photo stays to review: another candidate is credible.
set.auto_confirm_threshold.sub: Minimum confidence to confirm without review.
set.detect_groups.sub: Only these groups are detected and kept: fewer false positives, faster analysis. Unticking a group removes its detections awaiting review. Ticking it again does not re-analyze photos already processed (Re-analyze button in the viewer, or taxonero reanalyze all).
set.detection.sub: Automatic: the detectors look for subjects on every photo. Manual: no automatic detection, you draw the boxes yourself in the viewer and each one is identified right away. Switching to manual removes automatic detections still awaiting review; the ones you reviewed stay.
set.device.sub: The GPU is much faster. Results are the same on both: full-precision computation (float32, no TF32). Without a usable GPU, the CPU takes over.
set.exclude_extinct.sub: Species known mostly from fossils (prehistoric horses, dogs or camelids…). They mostly show up on photos without GPS.
set.full_image_fallback: Whole image when nothing is detected
set.full_image_fallback.sub: When no detector finds a subject, classify the whole photo anyway. Catches a few algae or lichens, but mostly produces false positives on photos without animals (landscapes, indoor shots) and slows the analysis down. The Identify page always does it.
set.gpu_batch.sub: Photos analysed together on the GPU. 0: automatic from its memory (8 for 12 GB), reduced on its own if it runs out. Larger: faster, but more memory. No effect on the CPU.
set.hide_absent: Exclude species absent from the region
set.hide_absent.sub: Geotagged photos: excludes species never observed within about 500 km (red badge). A rare or out-of-range species may then be missed.
set.interval_minutes.sub: Minutes between two checks for new photos in Immich.
set.lang.sub: Interface, species names and Wikipedia articles. Specific to this browser. Tags and descriptions written to Immich stay in {tags} ({env}).
set.models_idle_minutes.sub: Minutes without analysis before freeing GPU memory; reloaded for the next analysis. 0: always kept.
set.open_detector_mode.sub: OWLv2 is the slowest model on the CPU. As fallback: only when MegaDetector finds no animal in the photo. Auto: always on GPU, as fallback on CPU.
set.saved_device: Saved · models will be reloaded on the next analysis
set.saved_filters: Saved · applied to pending detections in the background
set.skip_people.sub: A photo where Immich recognized at least one person is not analyzed (portraits, family photos): far less computing and fewer false detections.
set.skip_raw_twins: Skip RAW files paired with a JPG
set.skip_raw_twins.sub: A RAW file paired with a JPG (or HEIC) of the same shot (same file name, same capture time) is not analyzed: it gets the JPG's tags. When off, the RAW is analyzed too (twice the computing for these shots).
set.write_description.sub: Adds a “Nature” block to the photo description in Immich (your text is never modified).

tree.info_body:
The tree follows GBIF's classification of life: each species belongs to ever broader groups, the taxonomic ranks.

  1. Kingdom (Animals, Plants, Fungi…)
  2. Phylum (Chordates, Arthropods…)
  3. Class (Birds, Mammals, Insects…)
  4. Order (Passerines, Carnivorans…)
  5. Family (Canids, Tits…)
  6. Genus, then species

Not every group has every rank in GBIF: bony fish have no class there, and some reptiles have no order. The missing level is shown as "No class in GBIF" (or order…), so each rank stays in its place. Group names are plural, species names singular.

undo.title: Undo what was written to Immich
undo.sub: Removes the tags set by the tool and its block in descriptions, then deletes its tags that became empty. Your photos, your text and your own tags are not touched. Your reviews stay in Taxonero.
undo.none: Nothing to remove: no recorded writes.
undo.dry: Test mode is on (DRY_RUN=true): removal is not possible while writing is disabled.
undo.warn: Writes are suspended first, otherwise the next cycle would put everything back. On a large library this can take a long time; if it stops, running it again resumes where it left off.

undo.remaining: {n} photo(s) still to clean: run the removal again.
undo.interrupted: Removal interrupted: run it again to resume.
undo.failed: Removal failed: {msg}. Run it again to resume.
undo.paused: Writes suspended: nothing is written to Immich any more.
undo.resume_hint: Resuming puts the tags and descriptions of all confirmed photos back over the next cycles.
